target_customer: Consumers asking health questions, plus healthcare businesses via API
problem: People and clinicians want direct, cited answers to medical questions instead of sifting search results.
business_model: Freemium consumer app with a Pro subscription and a business API

founders.name: Eduard Oravkin
founders.background_notes: YC page gives no background. One aggregator calls him a PhD student; not verified.

founders.name: Michal Pándy
founders.background_notes: No background found on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Retrieval over medical literature with LLM answers and citations; accuracy and safety were the hard parts in 2023.

defensibility.rationale: Built on public literature and third party LLMs, so copyable; no proprietary data evidenced.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Wolters Kluwer released UpToDate Expert AI in September 2025 per a review; no source shows an acquisition of MediSearch.

market_need_then: Large consumer volume of health searches and clinician demand for fast evidence; generative AI made direct answers possible in 2023.

branding.domain_note: Uses medisearch.io rather than .com; history not found.

identity.logo: Logo exists on Brandfetch; design not described
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, science focused with a not a substitute for a professional disclaimer

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name that says what it does but is generic; no brand press found.

outcome_analysis: MediSearch raised a 500K seed around mid 2023 and launched MediSearch Pro on web and mobile plus an API, staying a team of roughly six. Strong funded competitors such as OpenEvidence entered the same space, and no further rounds or exit are documented.
notes: Seed amount appears on CB Insights and SignalBase, both aggregators; investors vary by source (Pioneer Fund on CB Insights; YC and Continuity Fund on Bouncewatch, not recorded). HQ conflicts between London and San Francisco. Medwise.ai is a different company. No dated competitor source found, list left empty.
